scenario: G6 — Market value with a foreign holding
note: Hand-computed once and frozen. Changing a figure here requires a PR comment explaining why the previously verified number was wrong (TESTING.md §5).

fixture.note: The lot's fx_rate_to_base is fixed at acquisition and never revalued, so the cost figure carries 75 for ever. The market figure converts at the dated rate — which is why the two differ for FX reasons alone, independently of any price.

marketAtAugust3.note: VOO closes at $400 — exactly what it cost. The whole difference from the cost figure is the currency rebasis, which is the release-note fact ADR-23 requires stating.

marketAtAugust14.note: VOO 100 × $450 = $45,000 × 83 = 3,735,000; INFY 400 × 1,700 = 680,000. Cash is identical on both bases — a balance is a recorded fact, not a price.

restatementAtAugust14.note: FX rebasis: $40,000 of cost at 83 instead of 75 = +320,000. Price: VOO (3,735,000 − 3,320,000) + INFY (680,000 − 600,000) = +495,000. Both computed; neither is a residual.
